messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary error rate exceeded threshold for service `inference-api` in eu-west-1 during staged rollout (5% -> 18% over 3m). Auto-rollout did NOT trigger (metric window mismatch). Pager: @ryan_oncall :rotating_light:
Ryan (oncall): I'm on it. how bad is customer impact? any 5xx spikes or user-visible failures?
Sara (deploy): We're seeing ~12% 5xx for the canary subset (10% of traffic). Errors look like OOM/stream timeouts from the new quantization path. Non-canary traffic normal.
Nina (SRE): Thanks. Can you paste the deploy command / commit? I want to check canary config and autoscaler.
Sara (deploy): deploy-bot ran: ```deploy-bot: rollout start inference-api --image=redwood/inference:canary-2026-03-15-7f2a9c --canary=10% --region=eu-west-1``` commit 7f2a9c
Sam (QA): Reproduced a few timeouts locally with a short sequence (seq_len ~1024) hitting the quant path. Stacktrace shows kv-cache memory jump before crash.
Nina (SRE): Autoscaler didn't scale because mem metric threshold is under the radar for the canary size. Automated rollback condition was tied to 20% error; we were at 18% so it missed.
Ryan (oncall): Ok we need a manual rollback/kill-switch. Options: 1) flip feature flag to disable new quant path 2) roll back canary to previous image 3) scale down canary and divert traffic. Fastest?
Sara (deploy): Flag flip is fastest if it truly gates the quant path. Flag endpoint: `POST https://flags.redwood.internal/feature/inference/quant-v2/off` (auth header required). I can flip now.
Maria (PM): Customer impact: a few EU customers reported degraded responses; no major outages but latency and error SLOs drifting. Recommend short comms if we flip.
Nina (SRE): If flag flip is instantaneous, do that first. If errors persist, we rollback image. Also capture heap dumps before we restart pods.
Ryan (oncall): Sara, flip flag and confirm. Nina, prepare rollback steps if needed. Sam, collect sample logs and heap metric.
Sara (deploy): Flipping now... `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ****" https://flags.redwood.internal/feature/inference/quant-v2/off`
Sara (deploy): :white_check_mark: Flag flip acknowledged by feature-service.
incident-bot: NOTE: Feature flag change propagated to eu-west-1 within 8s.
Sam (QA): Seeing immediate drop in 5xx to ~3% in canary. Heap pressure dropping in the problematic pods.
Nina (SRE): Good. Let's hold 10m and observe. If stable, we won't rollback. Please run smoke checks and confirm token-level errors cleared.
Ryan (oncall): Running smoke now. `curl -s -X POST https://inference.eu-west-1.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'` -> OK.
Maria (PM): I'll draft a brief status update for affected customers: quick note about temporary degradation, mitigation via a config flip, and we're monitoring.
Sara (deploy): I'll create a revert PR to cut the canary change entirely and schedule a proper rollback on the rollout dashboard as a precaution.
Nina (SRE): Capture incident tags and add to postmortem queue if we still had SLO breaches after 30m.
Ryan (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. Leaving thread open for the 30m observation window. If no regressions, we'll resolve and write up follow-up actions (change auto-rollback threshold, add metric for mem-surge, ensure flag coverage). :thumbsup:
Sara (deploy): Noted. I'll also attach the heap dumps and logs to the ticket if we need deeper analysis.
Maria (PM): Thanks team.
Ryan (oncall): Closing thoughts: priority actions -> (1) add mem surge metric to rollback rules, (2) make canary autoscaler more sensitive to memory, (3) add end-to-end sims for quant path at seq_len 1024+.
incident-bot: Incident status: MITIGATED (pending 30m observation). Incident ID: INC-2026-0315-42
